## Introduction and Data Preparation

For this project, we will be looking at CDC data about Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART). This data provides information about fertility clinics across the United States in the years 2020-2022. Links to download each year of the data are provided below:

- [2020 data](https://data.cdc.gov/Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-/2020-Final-Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-Se/92ri-yjps/about_data)
- [2021 data](https://data.cdc.gov/Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-/2021-Final-Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-Se/ui6g-vumy/about_data)
- [2022 data](https://data.cdc.gov/Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-/2022-Final-Assisted-Reproductive-Technology-ART-Se/ix4g-rt8v/about_data)

### Libraries

First, load in all libraries that are needed for this data investigation.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(usmap)
```

### Read in Data

Read in each year of data and stack together into one data set.

```{r}
rawdata2020 <- read_csv("data/2020_Final_Assisted_Reproductive_Technology_(ART)_Services_and_Profiles_20261024.csv")

rawdata2021 <- read_csv("data/2021_Final_Assisted_Reproductive_Technology_(ART)_Services_and_Profiles_20261024.csv")

rawdata2022 <- read_csv("data/2022_Final_Assisted_Reproductive_Technology_(ART)_Services_and_Profiles_20261024.csv")

rawdata <- bind_rows(rawdata2020, rawdata2021, rawdata2022)

#view data
rawdata
```

### Data Cleaning

Validate that the variable `Topic` is "Clinic Services & Profile" and the variable `TopicId` is "TOP01" for all 17,012 records in the raw data, so these variables can be dropped.

```{r}
table(rawdata$Topic)
table(rawdata$TopicId)

rawdata |>
  select(-c("Topic", "TopicId"))
```

Remove summary rows from the data that do not correspond to a specific clinic.

```{r}
#view records to drop
rawdata |>
  select(-c("Topic", "TopicId")) |>
  filter(is.na(LocationAbbr))

#view records to keep
rawdata |>
  select(-c("Topic", "TopicId")) |>
  filter(!is.na(LocationAbbr))
```

Replace \* values with *NA*.

```{r}
rawdata |>
  select(-c("Topic", "TopicId")) |>
  filter(!is.na(LocationAbbr)) |>
  filter(Data_Value == "*") |> #for testing
  mutate(Data_Value = replace_values(Data_Value, from = "*", to = NA)) |>
  select(c("SubTopic", "Data_Value")) #for testing
```

Save the cleaned data up to this point (still long).

```{r}
longdata <- rawdata |>
  select(-c("Topic", "TopicId")) |>
  filter(!is.na(LocationAbbr)) |>
  mutate(Data_Value = replace_values(Data_Value, from = "*", to = NA)) |>
  arrange(SubTopicId)
```

Turn the data wide by subtopic.

```{r}
longdata |>
  select(-c("SubTopicId")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = SubTopic, values_from = Data_Value)
```

Convert variables to numeric or factors and store results.

```{r}
CDC <- longdata |>
  select(-c("SubTopicId")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = SubTopic, values_from = Data_Value) |>
  mutate(across(`Total cycles`:`Total infants born`, as.numeric)) |>
  mutate(across(`Donor egg services`:`Verified lab accreditation`, as.factor))

#view results
CDC

CDC |>
  select(`Total cycles`:`Total infants born`) #for testing

CDC |>
  select(`Donor egg services`:`Verified lab accreditation`) #for testing

#Save to rds file
write_rds(CDC, "data/Cleaned CDC data.rds")
```

## Data Investigation

### One-Way Contingency Tables

Use one-way contingency tables to display the number of clinics that fall within particular groups (as of a specific year).

```{r}
CDC |>
  filter(Year == 2022) |>
  group_by(`Donor egg services`) |>
  summarize(count = n())

CDC |>
  filter(Year == 2022) |>
  group_by(`Clinic Status`) |>
  summarize(count = n())
```

### Two-Way Contingency Tables

Use two-way contingency tables to display the number of clinics that fall within particular groups (as of a specific year).

```{r}
CDC |>
  filter(Year == 2022) |>
  group_by(`Donor egg services`, `Clinic Status`) |>
  summarize(count = n()) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Clinic Status`, values_from = count)
```

### Numerical Summaries

Numerical summaries (means, medians, sds, etc.) for quantitative variables at levels of categorical variables (as of a specific year).

```{r}
CDC |>
  filter(Year == 2022) |>
  group_by(`Gestational carrier services`) |>
  summarize(count = n(),
            across(c(Deliveries, `Total infants born`),
            list("mean" = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "median" = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "sd" = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                 "IQR" = ~ IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
            .names = "{.fn}_{.col}"))
```

### Plot 1: Bar Chart

```{r}

ggplot(data = CDC,
       aes(x = Year, fill = `Gestational carrier services`)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(y = "Number of Clinics") +
  theme_light()

```

### Plot 2: Smoothed Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(data = CDC |>
         filter(Year == 2022, Pregnancies < 1500) |>
         drop_na(Pregnancies)) +
  geom_density(aes(alpha = 0.5, x = Pregnancies,
                   fill = `Gestational carrier services`)) +
  theme_light()
```

### Plot 3: Box Plot

```{r}

ggplot(data = CDC |>
         filter(Year == 2022,
                LocationDesc %in% c("New York",
                                    "California",
                                    "North Carolina")),
       aes(x = LocationDesc, y = Pregnancies, fill = LocationDesc)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_light()

```

### Plot 4: Scatter Plot

```{r}
ggplot(data = CDC |>
         filter(Year == 2022,
                LocationDesc %in% c("New York",
                                    "California",
                                    "North Carolina"),
                `Total cycles` < 10000) |>
         drop_na(`Total cycles`, Pregnancies),
       aes(x = `Total cycles`, y = Pregnancies, color = LocationDesc)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = lm) + 
  theme_light()
```

### Plot 5: Faceted Smooth Histogram

```{r}
ggplot(data = CDC |>
         filter(Pregnancies < 1500) |>
         drop_na(Pregnancies)) +
  geom_density(aes(alpha = 0.5, x = Pregnancies,
                   fill = `Gestational carrier services`)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Year) +
  theme_light()
```

### Plot 6: Map

```{r}
plot_usmap(data = CDC |>
             filter(Year == 2022) |>
             drop_na(Pregnancies) |>
             rename(state = LocationAbbr) |>
             group_by(state) |>
             summarize(Pregnancies = sum(Pregnancies)),
           values = "Pregnancies",
           regions = "states") +
  scale_fill_continuous(low = "white", high = "red", name = "Pregnancies")
```
